title: Young bassist Buddy, criticism and his unchanged style
summary: He recalls trying to get Buddy to play bass the old way, why he never led a band, and his popularity from records worldwide.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Even Buddy. Of course Buddy don't date back with me. Buddy, because he's a latecomer. He's a latecomer. See, but Buddy's the same way. Man I was racing him and Mike here, and I was trying to get him to play the type of bass, you know what I mean? And he gets to play and he goes, that four, four beat, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, boom. Running all up and down the neck of the bass. Yeah, you see. Yeah.
Which is it. I think it looks good, but it doesn't get to be a band of the right support. No musician can't appreciate it.

There's somebody out there that knows what it's all about, they think he's racing sand, you know what I mean? Yeah. But I know better than you know better. See? And I tell him, he wouldn't tell me he didn't want to do it, but I can see his attitude, he become indignant, you know, about that. He's going, I'll catch it, I'll catch it, just go, I don't want that. If I'm rehearsing a band, let a man play like a talent, if I go ahead and play he'll catch it. You know what I'm telling me Bill? That's why I've never had no band. And see because if I'm going to rehearse a band, I mean play it the way I ask you to play. And any musician can do it. If you can play it all, you can play it. If you can play it double four beats, you can play it too. It's hard to be easy.

But those guys are afraid of criticism. Afraid they go somewhere and play like that, somebody's just going to come in and say they can't play. Well I'm not worrying about what the musician said because he doesn't mean anything to the band. Nine out of ten he comes in free. And when he gets in there he don't spend anything, he only comes there to criticize. You see what I mean? That's all he comes there to criticize. Either constructive or destructive, either one. If you're good he'll praise you, and if you're bad he'll talk about you.
But they're not the ones that support the band.

They're not the ones that support the band. They want to play. I'm playing for these people and I'm spending their money keeping their house open and paying my salary. And let's remember what the musicians are going to say about it. Eventually they will realize that the band can play. Maybe they'll not play to the first night to come in there. But if they keep coming, they'll eventually realize the band can play. You don't have to worry about that. Absolutely. You don't have to worry about it. But that's the trouble with the musician of today. I say even the older ones, Buddy is not an old musician, but he's an old man in the dance, in the music world. Before he played he's been going around to dances, and he ain't good bands, and he knows about good music. But they have that inferiority complex, afraid the other fellow will criticize them, they can't play. I still play the same way I played 40 years ago. And the people still like it.
It still sounds good to me and the people are still crazy about it. They'll give you a chance to hear you. That's right. They'll give you a chance to all through them at the end.
Oh, what? I mean, I have one style of playing, and it has made me very popular. Yeah, but it was good then.

I mean, I've seen names travel all over the world. As I say I've got correspondence here from Australia, Canada, Europe, Italy, France, Switzerland. I mean, the people I've never seen, they've never seen me. They only heard some of the records I worked on. And my playing attracted them to the extent where they wanted to correspond with me. So I mean, there must be something to it.
So why should I worry about another musician criticizing what I do?
